chapter: On the road with the Moores
title: Shelton Brooks coaches him in the wings
summary: After applause, Shelton Brooks, standing offstage, tells him how to bow and to ask the bandleader for the Bugle Call Rag.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, I didn't have those bottle tops on my feet this time, you see, on the stage, but I was barefooted, see. The people wanted to laugh, you see, and I didn't think really that I could dance, you know. I was just learning these steps, you see. So a fellow was standing in the wings offstage, and as I went off the stage and people was applauding and saying, more, more, dance, dance, you know, because they loved dancing in the South, you see, it was very popular. That was on account of Jack Wiggins, John Bowles, you know, Buckin' Bowles, and Walter Beatty and people like that, Mills, Buddy Bradley, Florence Meers, you know. It was kind of popular then, dancing, especially tap dancing.

And this fellow was standing offstage, and I knew who he was. They say he was Shelton Brooks, you know. So I didn't know his name at that time, and I asked him, I say, "Mister, I says -- what should I do?" And I had a big smile on my face, you see, and he said, "Well, you keep that smile on your face and just walk just off the curtain there and bend

over halfway to the people that's setting out there applauding for you. And you do the same thing, you turn to the -- see the gentleman with the stick in his hand that's down there leading the orchestra? I say, 'Yes, sir.'

He said, 'Well, you do the same thing to him, and then you turn back to the people and do it again to him. Then you come back off here to me, and I'll tell you what to do.' So that's what I did. Well, the people kept getting louder and louder, you know, and they say more, more, dance, dance. That was good, dance, dance, dance, and so on, you see.

So I say, 'Mister, what should I do now?' So he said, 'Well, you turn right around, and you walk up there to the middle of where you're singing and say what do you like, what's your favorite music?' So I says, 'Well, the Bugle Call Rag.' So he says, 'Good.' He say, 'Well, you walk up there in front of that gentleman that's got the stick in his hand and ask him to play the Bugle Call Rag.'

And I say, 'Yes, sir.' And I says, 'What do I do then?' you know. And he says, 'Well, go on out,' he says. 'Go over there, go up there and, if they say they know it, he then says, do what the people say, you know.' And they was saying, 'Dance, dance,' you know.
We like to see dancing, you see, you know. That's what I did.

I was game, you understand. So I figured that if my mother was out in the audience, you know, because my aunt says that when mama got home that she was going to tell her that I was going to be up on the stage at the theater, you see, the 81 Theater, you see. And I wanted to do anything, you know. I knew I could turn a handspring, see, at the time. And so --
